response: Yes, failures of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) are associated with steep posterior tibial slopes. Research has shown that both medial and lateral posterior tibial slopes (PTS) were significantly steeper in failures of ACLR compared to the control group. Specifically, a medial or lateral PTS of 5° or greater was identified as a new risk factor for ACLR failure. This suggests that steep posterior tibial slopes may be a contributing factor to the failure of ACL reconstruction.
